note: Q3 numbers are new and the company's own Q2-to-Q3 seasonality (+21%/+18% operating profit) sits well above the ~+10% QoQ the 3.27 consensus implies, with a September loan-book/FX tailwind on a line consensus under-called twice; thin capital headroom and rising credit losses are small offsets.

Booked 2026 revenue already above FY25 by mid-July favours an 'ahead' statement on a thin one-broker AIM name, but the bar is unsourced, this name has sold its 'ahead' updates, and it ran into the notice, so p_up stays near 50.
84% of the 30 Sep NAV is computable from public prices and already in the share price; only a small Instabee mark-up on 2.6% of NAV is open, so essentially a non-result.

FY26 is pre-released, so the move lives in the qualitative FY27 outlook, which starts from a June pre-buy and sticky input costs, plus a small audit-delay tail; the expected dividend raise is mostly priced.

FY26 and the first FY27 guide were both given four weeks ago; Bytes/Computacenter channel strength is a mild positive for the Q1 commentary, against a likely special-dividend cut and pull-forward comps, in a sector that sells good prints.

The strongest September since 2017 (SMMT, private +13.9%) against a JLR-depressed comp supports a firmer 'ahead' guide, while the stock has round-tripped the August upgrade to the buyback's ceiling; discount-led margins are the offset.
